title: Life Lessons Learned Through Contact Improvisation | Gregory Catellier & Kristin O'Neal | TEDxEmory

observation_window.sampling: provider default; not continuous motion capture

extraction.teacher_style: The teachers use a conversational, lecture-style approach to explain the concepts behind the movement. They alternate between speaking to the audience and demonstrating the dance steps together.

lesson_structure.note: The teachers perform a short contact improvisation sequence.
The teachers introduce themselves and the topic of contact improvisation.
The teachers explain the core concepts of contact improvisation, such as presence and touch.
The teachers provide a brief historical background of the dance form.
The teachers explain the concept of a 'jam' and 'kinesphere'.
The teachers explain and demonstrate 'reaching into negative space'.
The teachers explain and demonstrate 'sharing weight'.
The teachers discuss the 'soft skills' or 'power skills' learned through contact improvisation.
The teachers compare contact improvisation to a 'kinetic puzzle'.

metaphors: imaginary bubble that extends from your center
safety: avoid that couple and not hit our face on the wall

steps_taught.name: reaching into negative space
steps_taught.description: Reaching into the space inside the kinesphere where your body is not.

steps_taught.name: sharing weight
steps_taught.description: Leaning on your partner to find a momentary balance.

what_works: The teachers use clear, descriptive language to explain abstract concepts.
The teachers demonstrate the concepts in real-time, making them easier to understand.
what_hinders: The lesson is more of a lecture than a practical, step-by-step tutorial.

quotes.text: Contact improvisation demands that you be completely present with another human.
Kinesphere is the imaginary bubble that extends from your center to your distal ends.
It's the space inside the kinesphere where your body is not.
Every contact dance is a little kinetic puzzle.

evidence_segments.observation: The teachers perform a series of fluid, improvised movements, including lifts and weight-sharing.
The teacher explains the concept of 'kinesphere' while gesturing to the space around their body.
The teacher demonstrates 'reaching into negative space' by extending an arm into the space near their partner.
The teachers demonstrate 'sharing weight' by leaning against each other.

extraction.distinctive_method: The teachers use a lecture-based approach to teach the philosophy and concepts of contact improvisation, rather than focusing on specific steps or sequences.
